title: The Frog-King, or Iron Henry
source: Grimm, Household Tales, tr. Margaret Hunt (1884), tale 1
lesson: Keep your promises, even the inconvenient ones.
lines: In the original story, the princess never kisses the frog. A princess was playing by a forest well, when her golden ball fell in.
A frog popped up. I'll fetch it, if I may be your friend, eat from your golden plate, and sleep in your little bed.
Yes, anything! she said. He fetched it. She ran off.
Next evening, at dinner: knock, knock. Princess, youngest princess, open the door for me! The King frowned. What you have promised, you must perform.
So the frog ate from her plate, then demanded to be carried upstairs. At last she lost her temper, and flung him at the wall.
Flash! A handsome prince stood there, freed from a witch's spell.
His servant, Faithful Henry, was so happy that the iron bands round his heart snapped. Keep your promises, even the inconvenient ones.
Next time: a cat and a mouse share a pot of fat. Follow so you don't miss it!
